Package com.bilt.pos.session

Class SessionBasket

java.lang.Object
com.bilt.pos.session.SessionBasket
public final class SessionBasket extends Object
The basket surface of a shopper session: item and tax mutations, batch edits, whole-basket replacement, and immutable snapshots. Sale, return, and register-credit items can coexist in one basket.

There is one basket and three ways to update it. They are different updaters over the same engine, not different concepts: every one of them applies atomically, returns the updated snapshot synchronously, and ends in exactly one BasketChange notification (which, on a terminal session with automatic display enabled, enqueues one asynchronous, conflated customer display refresh).

Incremental (BasketChange.Source.INCREMENTAL): one call per register action, for a POS that rings items as the cashier scans them. 


 session.basket().addItem(
     BasketItem.sale("KRK-CNDL-LRG-VAN", "Large Vanilla Candle", 2, new BigDecimal("24.99")));
 session.basket().updateItemQuantityBySku("KRK-CNDL-LRG-VAN", 3);
 session.basket().setTaxRateBySku("KRK-CNDL-LRG-VAN", new BigDecimal("0.08875"));

Batched (BasketChange.Source.BATCH): several mutations applied as one atomic change, for a register action that touches more than one line. 


 session.basket().mutate(m -> m
     .addItem(BasketItem.sale("KRK-FRAME-5X7-BLK", "5x7 Black Frame", 1, new BigDecimal("14.99")))
     .removeItemBySku("KRK-CNDL-LRG-VAN")
     .setTaxTotal(new BigDecimal("1.33")));

Snapshot (BasketChange.Source.REPLACE): the whole basket at once, for a POS that owns its own cart and would rather push its current state after every change than translate each edit into incremental calls. The session diffs the snapshot against the current basket, so downstream consumers still learn what changed. 


 List<BasketItem> items =
     pos.cart().lines().stream().map(Mapping::toBasketItem).collect(Collectors.toList());
 session.basket().replace(items);
 // or, with a Basket the register assembled or received earlier:
 session.basket().replace(snapshot);

The owning session decides when updates are allowed: a basket frozen by in-flight money movement, already consumed by settlement, or owned by an ended session rejects them with IllegalStateException. Call clear() after settlement to start another basket in the same session; replace(Basket) does that implicitly on a consumed basket.

Like the session that owns it, the basket is intended for use from a single register thread.

    • snapshot

      public Basket snapshot()
      An immutable snapshot of the current basket.

    • clear

      public Basket clear()
      Clears all items and tax, starts a fresh basket with a new cart ID, and clears the stored-value card selected for split tender.

      This is the explicit transaction boundary for a session that runs more than one settlement. A settled basket cannot be charged again; clear it before ringing the next one. Clearing never abandons financial recovery. When recovery cannot be completed, call TerminalShopperSession.forceEnd(String) and start a new session rather than reusing this basket.

      Returns:
      the new empty basket snapshot
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if money movement, settlement recovery, or a partially completed same-session void is still in progress, or the session has ended

    • replace

      public Basket replace(Basket snapshot)
      Replaces the whole basket with a snapshot: the session basket becomes equal to the snapshot's lines, discounts, taxes and tax total, and the change is reported as one BasketChange.Source.REPLACE diff against the previous basket. A snapshot equal to the current basket produces an empty diff and no notification, and so no display push.

      Lines are paired with the current basket the way the basket keys them, by reference when a line has one and otherwise by SKU and item type among the unreferenced lines; a paired line keeps its item id, so register references into the basket stay stable, while new lines get new ids. Each snapshot line needs a SKU, description, unit price and a quantity of at least one, like a BasketItem. Line tax follows the snapshot line (a taxRate makes it rate-based, a disagreeing or rate-less non-zero taxAmount fixes it), and the snapshot's taxTotal becomes a basket-level override only when it differs from the sum of its lines' tax amounts.

      On a terminal session whose basket has been consumed by a successful settlement, replace does not fail the way an incremental mutation does: it starts a fresh cart with a new cart id exactly as clear() would (same guards, and the split-tender stored-value selection is dropped) and then installs the snapshot, reporting every line as added.

      Returns:
      the updated basket snapshot
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the snapshot holds two unreferenced lines with the same SKU and type or two lines with the same reference, or a line fails item validation; the basket is left untouched
      IllegalStateException - if the basket is frozen (payment in progress) or the session has ended, or, for a consumed basket, under the clear() guards

    • replace

      public Basket replace(List<BasketItem> items)
      Replaces the whole basket with register items, the common shape of a POS-owned cart: the basket becomes exactly these lines, paired with the current ones and reported as in replace(Basket). Tax comes from the items' own taxRate/taxAmount; a basket-level setTaxTotal(java.math.BigDecimal) override already in place is kept when no item carries tax and dropped when any does, so a register that taxes the whole basket sets the total once and keeps replacing items.
      Returns:
      the updated basket snapshot
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if two items share a reference, or two unreferenced items share a SKU and type; the basket is left untouched
      IllegalStateException - under the same rules as replace(Basket)
